newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ekran revises Bakun share offer structure.
newsitem.headline: Ekran revises Bakun share offer structure.

text.p: Ekran Bhd, the main contractor for the $5.5 billion Bakun hydroelectric dam, said on Tuesday it was revising the dam holding company's share offer structure to include a 1.5 billion rights issue.

Ekran's executive chairman Ting Pek Khiing told reporters following the company's annual general meeting that the stock offering for Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp Bhd will still include a listing of 1.5 billion shares at 2.00 ringgit a share.
He said this stock listing could be done "perhaps in the next month". The Securities Commission is currently considering the Bakun company listing application.
Ting said the rights offering will take place about a year after the stock offering, on the basis of one new share for every existing share at 2.00 ringgit a piece.
In total, the issues will raise six billion ringgit. "To cover the balance of the contract's cost, we will find the best instrument at the least interest expense," Ting told reporters.

Work on the dam, located in the jungles of Sarawak state on Borneo island, began on December 1, and the company foresees no delays, Ting said. The 2,400 megawatt capacity dam is set to start generating power by 2003.
Earlier on Tuesday, Bakun received two licences from Malaysia's Ministry of Energy, Telecommunications and Posts related to the project.
It was granted a licence to generate, transmit and supply electricity as well as a licence to transmit the power via an undersea cable to peninsular Malaysia.

Energy Telecommunications and Posts Minister Leo Moggie said in a speech on Tuesday that the licences covered the dam's construction, expected to be no longer than six years, and operations for 30 years.
Moggie said completion of the project was expected not later than August 31, 2003.
"This (licensing) has made us a legal electricity producer," Ting told reporters.

The Ekran head said the lead underwriter for the Bakun share offering to Malaysian investors is Commerce International Merchant Bankers Bhd. About 10 percent of Bakun's stock will also be offered to foreign investors. Ting said an underwriter for the foreign tranche has not yet been selected.
Ekran director Peter Ling said he expected the return-on-equity in the Bakun stock to be about 12 percent.
Asked about his health, Ting, who had a mild stroke in September, said, "I'm healthier than before."
